clue.text: Agree to dog tracking prisoner

indicators.note: to track something is to follow behind it, so the dog comes after the prisoner

parts.note: a con is short for a convict
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone consents to letting a dog follow an escaped prisoner's trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is a formal synonym for being of the same opinion as someone.

clue.text: Instrument initially owned by Offenbach and Elgar

indicators.note: applies to each following word, so only the opening letter of each composer phrase word counts

parts.note: the opening letters of owned, by and Offenbach
the opening letter of the composer's name, after the link and

explanation.surface: A musical instrument once belonged to two famous composers, Offenbach and Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'and' is skipped: only owned, by, Offenbach and Elgar give their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument found in every orchestra.

clue.text: Opponent in fight with soldier

parts.note: combat is fighting between armed forces
a soldier ant is a caste of ant, so ant stands for soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone is an enemy in a battle alongside a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A soldier here is the insect: soldier ants guard the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is anyone engaged in fighting, so an adversary or opposing party.

clue.text: Write again about style

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a type is a kind or style of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to rewrite something concerning its style.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to key a document in a second time, a way of producing it once more.

clue.text: Stubborn about red version

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering of something, so these letters appear in a new order

parts.note: both words taken as written to supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone digs their heels in over a red edition of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a link or reversal sign but is simply part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate describes someone obstinately refusing to change their mind, a close synonym.

clue.text: Hardly ever does one see one columbine on a composition

indicators.note: a composition puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the flower's name, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is rare to see a columbine flower featured in a painting or piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does one see' is linking surface; the rearranged letters come only from one, columbine, on and a.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something occurring very rarely, as a second full moon in one month does.

clue.text: At a lower level, fell into decline

parts.note: down means below or lower
a fell is a hill or moorland upland in northern England

explanation.surface: Something dropped to a lower point and fell into a decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' reads as a verb but is the northern English noun for a hill. 'At a lower level' looks like the definition but supplies the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downhill is the idiom for deteriorating, so the word works as an adverb meaning toward decline.

clue.text: Student escaped jailor drunk with Spanish wine

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the student has got away, so that letter leaves the word jailor

parts.note: taken as written before the student leaves
L is a learner, as on a British learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A learner gets away from a jailer who is drunk on Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine region of northern Spain and the wine made there.

clue.text: Let nothing unusual restrict forbearance

indicators.note: unusual signals a strange new form, so let plus the zero are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is the round shape of zero
to ration is to limit supply

explanation.surface: An instruction not to let anything odd limit one's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Toleration is the act of putting up with things, which is what forbearance means: patient restraint.

clue.text: Paint alien in cosmic setting

indicators.note: the alien sits in the other word, which wraps around it
a setting holds something in place, as a ring holds a jewel, so cosmic surrounds the alien

parts.note: taken as written, then split around the alien
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A painting depicting an alien against a cosmic backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' here is make-up, not artist's paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is an old, somewhat disparaging word for make-up, which is a cosmetic.

clue.text: Jumper was confused

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted sweater, called a jumper in Britain
second meaning: ... thinking is vague and muddled

explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a pullover sweater, not someone who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a knitted garment; as an adjective it means vague or muddled in thought.

clue.text: Morning hip replacement drama produced in the auditorium

indicators.note: a replacement hip fits the earlier word, and replacing its parts puts them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
theatre is drama as an art form

explanation.surface: A morning hip operation is staged as a drama before an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip replacement' reads as the operation, but only replacement is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is a large open-air venue with tiered seating, a kind of auditorium.

clue.text: Rule intended, say, for Parliament

parts.note: to govern is to rule a country

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A statement of what a rule was intended to do for Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, the governing body of a country, which in Britain sits in Parliament.

clue.text: 1-0 to Agassi initially, leading to a scrap

parts.note: the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

indicators.note: applies to both words that follow, taking their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of to and Agassi

explanation.surface: A tennis match score of 1-0 to Andre Agassi leads to a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight in this sporting scene, but it means a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, means a very small amount or jot.

clue.text: A sign we are told to find after the French turn back

definitions.note: said aloud, a sign is assign, which means allot

indicators.note: find comes after the reversed article
turn back has the French word read in the opposite direction

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to locate is to find

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look for a sign after the French turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sound pun: 'a sign', spoken, is the verb assign.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign tasks or money is to allot or share them out, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Offspring of American gangster in early years

parts.note: a child is a son or daughter
hood is US slang for a hoodlum

explanation.surface: The son or daughter of a US gangster during their formative years.
explanation.definitionFit: Childhood is the period of life before adulthood, a person's earliest stage.

clue.text: Reckon to get bad value at the end

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so value and at are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of the word the is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone expects to get poor value in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end' looks like a phrase, but 'at' joins the jumble and 'the end' is a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to assess or estimate, which is one sense of reckon.

clue.text: Elvis gets fat when drunk on holiday

indicators.note: drunk suggests stagger and disorder, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the singer's name, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elvis puts on weight when he drinks on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like a description of Elvis but its letters join his name in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a day or period of celebration, an older sense of holiday as holy day.

clue.text: Bent coin showing a religious symbol

indicators.note: a bent object has been twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bent coin shows a religious emblem on its face.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred image, especially in the Orthodox church, used as a devotional emblem.

clue.text: Urge to get trophy, though it's something quite small

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: Someone is driven to win a trophy, though only a minor one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is vague on purpose: a cup that is small rather than a grand trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: An eggcup is a tiny cup for holding a boiled egg, a modestly sized container.

clue.text: That the United Nations was tested is not disputed

parts.note: UN is the standard short form of the international body
to be challenged is to be put to the test

explanation.surface: Nobody denies that the United Nations was put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchallenged has not been questioned or contested by anyone.

clue.text: One detests moving earth

indicators.note: moving the parts around gives a new arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the act of shifting soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater is a person who detests something, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: Sharp cry

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to wail in grief

explanation.walkthrough: Reads like a single sharp shout, but these are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means having a fine cutting edge; the verb means to lament loudly for the dead.

clue.text: A lady's collar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woman's name, with the apostrophe s as a link
second meaning: a wide, deep collar on a dress

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a woman's collar, but the woman's name is one meaning and the collar another.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female given name and also a broad lace collar worn around a low neckline.

clue.text: Kind of examination that can be violent

definitions.text: Kind of examination that can be violent

parts.note: a quick, cursory inspection of someone or something
in slang, giving someone this also means beating them up

explanation.walkthrough: A brief look over and, in slang, a roughing-up are both known by the same hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a rapid appraisal, and informally a physical beating.

clue.text: Surgeon takes time to fish

indicators.note: the surgeon takes in the letter for time, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written, then opened to take in the time

explanation.surface: A surgeon spends some time going fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish famous as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Teacher panted excitedly

indicators.note: excitement throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster was out of breath with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedant originally meant a schoolmaster, before taking its modern sense of a fussy stickler.
